prompts.display_text: Pin a country where a temple was dedicated in 2024.
prompts.text_original: A country where a temple was dedicated in 2024.
prompts.citation: Church temple list (original dedication dates), 26 Oct 2026
prompts.summary: In 2024 the Church dedicated new temples across the Americas and Asia. Argentina gained two, Salta and Mendoza, and others were dedicated in Puebla Mexico, Salvador Brazil, Lima Peru Los Olivos, Urdaneta Philippines, San Pedro Sula Honduras and Cobán Guatemala. The United States had eight, including Deseret Peak, Taylorsville and Orem in Utah.

answers.name: United States
answers.fact: Deseret Peak Utah, Taylorsville Utah, Orem Utah and 5 more dedicated in 2024.

answers.fact: Salvador Brazil dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Mexico
answers.fact: Puebla Mexico dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Argentina
answers.fact: Salta Argentina, Mendoza Argentina dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Peru
answers.fact: Lima Peru Los Olivos dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Urdaneta Philippines dedicated in 2024.

answers.name: Guatemala

answers.name: Honduras
answers.fact: San Pedro Sula Honduras dedicated in 2024.

prompts.display_text: Pin one of the 5 Asian countries Church History Topics names where servicemembers helped introduce the Church after World War II.
prompts.text_original: After World War II, Latter-day Saint servicemembers helped introduce or reestablish the Church in Asian countries where they were stationed. Pin one of the countries Church History Topics names.
prompts.citation: Church History Topics: Globalization; Growth of Missionary Work
prompts.summary: Church History Topics credits American Latter-day Saint servicemembers stationed abroad after World War II with helping introduce or reestablish the Church, especially in Japan, Korea, the Philippines, Vietnam and Thailand. Their servicemen's groups often grew into the first local branches.

answers.name: Japan
answers.fact: Named; servicemembers met in postwar Japan (Saints vol. 3 ch. 31).

answers.name: South Korea
answers.fact: Named; Korean War servicemen helped plant the Church.

answers.name: Philippines
answers.fact: Named; servicemen met in the Philippines after the war.

answers.name: Thailand
answers.fact: Named among countries where servicemembers helped establish the Church.

answers.name: Vietnam
answers.fact: Named; servicemember groups met there during the Vietnam War.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding a place in Jeremiah 39-44, from Jerusalem's fall to the flight into Egypt
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding a place in Jeremiah 39-44, from the fall of Jerusalem to the flight into Egypt: Zedekiah judged at Riblah, captives taken to Babylon, Jeremiah freed at Ramah, Gedaliah at Mizpah, Ishmael's flight to the Ammonites, and the remnant's settlements at Tahpanhes and Pathros
prompts.note: Ramah, Mizpah and Gibeon are in the West Bank (Palestine). Jerusalem is scored as Israel, as in the other Bible prompts.
prompts.summary: After Babylon broke into Jerusalem, Zedekiah was blinded at Riblah and taken to Babylon. Jeremiah, freed at Ramah, stayed with the governor Gedaliah at Mizpah until Ishmael, sent by the Ammonite king, murdered him. Fearing Babylon, the remnant fled to Egypt and took Jeremiah with them to Tahpanhes (Jer 39-44).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Against Jeremiah's word the remnant went to Tahpanhes, and Jews dwelt at Migdol, Noph and Pathros (Jer 43:7; 44:1).

answers.name: Iraq
answers.fact: Zedekiah was bound and carried to Babylon, with the rest of the people (Jer 39:7-9).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Jerusalem was broken up in Zedekiah's eleventh year (Jer 39:2).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: Zedekiah was overtaken in the plains of Jericho, and mourners came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria; Jeremiah was loosed at Ramah and went to Gedaliah at Mizpah (Jer 39:5; 40:1, 6; 41:5).

answers.name: Jordan
answers.fact: Baalis king of the Ammonites sent Ishmael to slay Gedaliah, and Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites (Jer 40:14; 41:15); Jews returned from Moab, Ammon and Edom to Gedaliah (Jer 40:11).

answers.name: Syria
answers.fact: Nebuchadrezzar judged Zedekiah at Riblah in the land of Hamath (Jer 39:5).

prompts.display_text: Pin a European country (Turkey counts) where Church histories place the first convert baptism on its soil in 1883-1899
prompts.text_original: A European country (Turkey counts) whose first convert baptism on its soil, per Church histories, came between 1883 and 1899.
prompts.citation: Church Global Histories chronologies: Austria, Czech Republic, Belgium, Russia, Romania; Church News country profile and Church History Topics: Turkey
prompts.note: Poland, Hungary and Serbia do not count: their first converts were baptized outside their borders.
prompts.summary: In the 1880s and 1890s missionaries carried the gospel into new corners of Europe. Church histories date first baptisms to Lambach, Austria (1883), Prague (1884), Constantinople (1885), Antwerp (1888), St. Petersburg (1895) and Constanta, Romania (1899).

answers.name: Austria
answers.fact: 1883: first convert baptism in Austria, at Lambach.

answers.name: Russia
answers.fact: 1895: first convert baptism in St. Petersburg.

answers.name: Belgium
answers.fact: 1888: first convert baptism in Belgium, at Antwerp.

answers.name: Czech Republic
answers.fact: 1884: first convert baptized in Prague.

answers.name: Turkey
answers.fact: January 4, 1885: Hagop Vartooguian and his family were baptized in Constantinople by Jacob Spori, days after the Turkish Mission opened.

answers.name: Romania
answers.fact: 1899: first convert baptized at Constanta on the Black Sea.

prompts.display_text: Pin a country holding one of Rehoboam's fenced cities, or a homeland of Shishak's army
prompts.text_original: A present-day country holding one of Rehoboam's fenced cities of Judah (2 Chronicles 11:5-10) or the homeland of a people in Shishak's army that came against him (2 Chronicles 12:2-3: Egyptians, Lubims, and the people of Cush, the Nile land south of Egypt)
prompts.note: Bible Ethiopia (Cush) lay in today's Sudan, so Ethiopia does not count. Bethlehem, Tekoa and Hebron are in the West Bank.
prompts.summary: After the kingdom split, Rehoboam built a ring of fenced cities to guard Judah, from Bethlehem and Hebron to Lachish and Aijalon. Because Judah forsook the law, Shishak of Egypt came with chariots and a host of Lubims, Sukkiims and Ethiopians, took the fenced cities and carried off the temple treasures (2 Chr 11-12).

answers.name: Egypt
answers.fact: Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem in Rehoboam's fifth year (2 Chr 12:2).

answers.name: Israel
answers.fact: Rehoboam fortified Lachish, Azekah, Adullam, Gath, Zorah and Aijalon (2 Chr 11:7-10).

answers.name: Palestine
answers.fact: He also fortified Bethlehem, Tekoa, Beth-zur and Hebron (2 Chr 11:6-10).

answers.name: Libya
answers.fact: The Lubims marched with Shishak (2 Chr 12:3); the Church footnote reads Libyans, and BD Libya is the land west of Egypt.

answers.name: Sudan
answers.fact: The Ethiopians marched with him too (2 Chr 12:3); Bible Ethiopia was the Nile land south of Egypt.
